issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new behavior, directly violating the project's test-first rule and leaving the required unauthorized-call and tamper tests for submit()/Dashboard entirely absent.

The public Entity $entity property is not #[Locked] and authorization only happens in mount(), so a client that swaps the model key on a later request can render another entity's name without being a member.
entity.pick performs its authorization with an inline membershipFor() check instead of a policy/gate, contrary to the convention that authorization always goes through app/Policies.
Creating an entity plus its owner membership is a domain write performed in the Livewire component rather than an app/Actions class with authorization inside it.
The 0 -> onboarding, 1 -> set session + dashboard, >1 -> switcher dispatch is duplicated verbatim in the middleware and the /home closure, so the two can drift apart.

Memberships are not filtered by the entity's soft-deleted state, so a user whose only entity was soft-deleted hits the count===1 branch with a null entity and fails route generation/context resolution instead of reaching onboarding.
isUniqueViolation() treats any SQLSTATE 23000 or message containing 'unique'/'duplicate' as a slug collision, so unrelated integrity errors are retried five times before surfacing.
The navbar runs a fresh memberships count query on every authenticated page render; caching it (e.g. once per request) would avoid the repeated query.
Slug uniqueness in the factory relies on a 5-digit random suffix and is not guaranteed, which can produce rare collisions in tests.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership data model, one-owner DB invariant, policies, tenant middleware, onboarding, dashboard, switcher, navbar entry, routes, lang keys and docs largely as specified. It cannot be approved yet: it ships no tests at all, the Dashboard exposes an unlocked public entity model that can be swapped client-side, and a few conventions (Actions, policy-based authorization) and soft-delete edge cases are not handled.
